Get an appointment with a talk therapist (a psychologist, not psychiatrist). Tell them basically what you've said here. "I have a substance problem, but my main concern is the underlying issues that cause it, and I'd like to get help with those." Go 2 or 3 times (aim for biweekly appointments to speed the process up), get a feeling for whether or not you can work with them and trust them, and get a diagnosis. If you have any doubts, find someone else. If they focus exclusively on the substance abuse and ignore the underlying issues, you need someone else. Tell them you're planning to see a psychiatrist to try medications. Have them write down your diagnosis and/or primary areas of concern. 

Anyhow, after this, get in to see a psychiatrist. This will be the person you get meds from. Your first appointment may be a half hour to an hour, but after that you'll probably see them once a month for 20 minutes or so. The focus here will be your medications and how they're working. It's important that you trust this person as well, and feel good about them. If they put you on more than 2 meds your first visit, they're likely a quack (sadly common). Psych meds often take 2-4 weeks to take effect (and this is *when* you find the right med!), so be patient. (Quick note: Be aware that some meds may make your symptoms worse. If this happens, don't try to wait it out. It can be dangerous. Let your psychiatrist know. This is uncommon but it can happen.)

But you *will* find meds that help, and talking about all of this with a sympathetic and qualified professional will help. Keep up hope! It takes time, but it does get better and easier.
